messages:
sophie: Heads-up — Acme (customer) is seeing chat SSE streams stop emitting after ~3-5s of idle. Works fine when they hit our hosted endpoint directly, only fails when routed through their nginx. They say the client sees a partial message, then nothing until connection close. Req id from our side: rdw-req-0a1b2c3d4e. Sample logs and repro below. Asking for repro steps we can give them.

mike: Can you paste the exact curl they used and the nginx proxy conf they have? Also need the timestamps for the failing requests so we can cross-check traces.

sophie: Their curl (sanitized):
```
curl -i -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \\  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\  -d '{"model":"redwood-1.2","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"stream test"}],"stream":true}' \\  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/stream"
```
They said they run this from behind nginx as a reverse proxy. Nginx snippet they provided: (sanitized)
```
location /chat/stream/ {
  proxy_pass https://api.redwood.example/;
  proxy_http_version 1.1;
  proxy_set_header Connection "";
  proxy_buffering on;
  proxy_buffers 8 16k;
}
```
They also have gzip on and some custom timeout values.

jules: This looks like classic proxy buffering/idle-window behavior. Nginx will buffer upstream responses until buffers are full or the stream is complete. For SSE/websocket-ish streaming we usually want:
- proxy_buffering off;
- proxy_request_buffering off;
- proxy_http_version 1.1;
- chunked_transfer_encoding on;
- set header to disable accel buffering: add_header X-Accel-Buffering no;
Also ensure gzip is disabled for that location (gzip off) because it forces buffering. Suggest they try adding those and re-test.

mike: If you can get them to run two quick repros that will tell us where it's happening:
1) curl directly to api.redwood.example (bypass nginx) with same flags and --no-buffer (-N).
2) curl to their nginx (same host) with -v and --no-buffer.
Also ask for nginx access + error log lines for the req id and the upstream response time window. If possible tcpdump of the client->nginx and nginx->upstream around the timestamps.

sophie: Provided minimal sanitized logs from our side for rdw-req-0a1b2c3d4e:
```
2026-03-10T18:12:34.112Z rdw-req-0a1b2c3d4e INFO stream.start model=redwood-1.2
2026-03-10T18:12:34.280Z rdw-req-0a1b2c3d4e INFO chunk.send seq=1 size=512
2026-03-10T18:12:36.785Z rdw-req-0a1b2c3d4e INFO chunk.send seq=2 size=128
2026-03-10T18:12:39.991Z rdw-req-0a1b2c3d4e INFO chunk.send seq=3 size=64
2026-03-10T18:12:44.120Z rdw-req-0a1b2c3d4e INFO stream.idle_detect idle_ms=5000
2026-03-10T18:12:44.121Z rdw-req-0a1b2c3d4e INFO connection.closed by_peer=false reason=client_read_timeout?
```
They say nginx shows the client connection stayed open but no bytes forwarded after seq=3.

jules: That pattern fits buffering at the proxy (first few small chunks get buffered then nginx doesn't flush until buffer threshold or a CRLF flush). Quick tests for the customer:
- Add `proxy_buffering off; proxy_request_buffering off; add_header X-Accel-Buffering no; gzip off;` to the location and reload.
- Re-run the curl with `curl -v -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" ...` and capture full verbose output (headers and timing).
- Run `tcpdump -i any -s 0 -w /tmp/nginx-to-upstream.pcap tcp and host <api.redwood.example>` while reproducing, and `tcpdump` on client side.

mike: Also ask them to try sending the header `X-Accel-Buffering: no` from the client (if they control the proxy rules) as a quick toggle. If they can't change nginx config, remind them that some managed proxies (CDNs) will still buffer and you need a different path.

support-bot: Created SR-45892 in tracker and attached initial logs/req id rdw-req-0a1b2c3d4e. Tagging streaming-partial-output.

sophie: I'm going to send the above recommended steps to the customer. For convenience, here's a short set of repro commands they can run and paste back: 
```
# direct (bypass proxy)
curl -i -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \\  -d '{"model":"redwood-1.2","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"stream":true}' \\  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/stream"

# via nginx (verbose)
curl -v -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \\  -d '{"model":"redwood-1.2","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"stream":true}' \\  "https://their-proxy.example/chat/stream/"

# tcpdump (run on nginx host)
sudo tcpdump -i any -s 0 -w /tmp/nginx-client-upstream.pcap tcp and host api.redwood.example
```

jules: Nice. Also request their nginx conf file and full access/error logs for the time window 2026-03-10T18:12:30 -> 2026-03-10T18:12:50. That'll let us verify whether nginx forwarded chunks or suppressed them.

sophie: OK I'll send these to Acme and ask for the debug bundle (nginx conf, access+error logs, the two curl outputs, and tcpdump pcap). Will follow up when they respond. :thumbsup:
